_README: CENSUS OF EVERY OBSERVER IN THIS REPO THAT DECIDES WHETHER SOMETHING ELSE IS ALIVE.
Enforced by tests/test_observer_contract.py. You do not opt in to this file and you
cannot forget it: the harness DISCOVERS its own subjects from the source tree by two
structural rules and fails on anything it finds that is not listed here.
Rule A (risk)     — a file under scripts/ or dashboard/ that identifies a process by
name/argv (pgrep, pidof, ps -e, ps aux) must appear below.
Rule B (adoption) — a file that sources observer_guard.sh must appear below with
contract 'v1', which subjects it to the behavioural battery.
contract values:
v1        — adopted. Exposes `<script> observe` printing state=present|absent|
unobservable and exiting 0|1|3. The harness runs the full battery
against it, including that it SUPPRESSES corrective action while blind
and still ACTS when the target is genuinely absent.
unadopted — a known instance of the defect class, not yet migrated. MUST name an
owning handoff and a task marker; the harness verifies an UNCHECKED
'- [ ]' line carrying that marker really exists in that file. A deferral
that is checked off or deleted without the migration turns this suite
RED. Deferring is allowed; deferring silently is not.
exempt    — reviewed and out of scope, with the reason recorded. Reviewed, not
forgotten: the row is the review.
Origin: 2026-08-12. bus_supervisor.sh identified the coordinator-daemon with
`pgrep -f 'session_bus_coordinator\.py run'`; the live daemon's argv had
'--bus-root <path>' between '.py' and 'run'. The pattern matched nothing, the
watchdog declared a healthy heartbeating daemon dead FOREVER, and relaunch-looped
for hours with nobody watching. Two signals were available and it required BOTH, so
the working one was overruled by the broken one and 'cannot tell' became 'dead'.

_adoption_pattern_note: An actual `source` statement, not any MENTION of the file. Matching a bare
mention flagged this contract's own census module for quoting the library's path
in its docstring — a guard tripping on prose about itself. Rule A stays a plain
mention match on purpose: writing `pgrep` in a scripts/ file is worth a moment's
thought even in a comment, and the one file that discusses it at length is listed
_roots_note: artifacts/operator/ is deliberately OUT of discovery scope: those are one-shot
ratifiers a human runs and reads once, not long-running observers whose verdict
nobody sees. Two of them do gate on an argv pattern and are recorded below as
'exempt' rows with the reason, so the finding is not lost — but a new ratifier
must not turn this suite red on an unrelated commit. A guard that forbids its own
neighbours' idiom gets deleted by the first person it blocks.
_self_exclude_note: The contract library itself. It matches Rule A only because its header QUOTES the
specimen's `pgrep -f` line while explaining why that shape is forbidden. Excluding it
by data, not by a special case in the test — and only this one file, so a second
'explanatory' mention elsewhere still trips the rule.

observers.notes: Reference adoption. Was the exact twin of the specimen: `runner_pids() { pgrep -f "$RUNNER_PATTERN"; }` + `[[ -n "$(runner_pids)" ]] && (( age <= STALE_AFTER ))`, and it kill -9'd every pid the pattern returned, on a shared host, on a boolean that could not distinguish dead from unseen. Its runner already published its own pid in heartbeat.json and the supervisor did not read it.

THE SPECIMEN. Being repaired in a parallel session (C49) as this row is written — the repair replaces the pattern with the heartbeat pid, which removes the instance. This row keeps the FILE enrolled so the class stays enforced afterwards: adopting observer_guard.sh + an `observe` entrypoint is what subjects it to the battery. Not edited from here; the file has a live owner.

Identity is correctly port-based (it already migrated off `pgrep -f 'dashboard\.server .*--port 8100'`) and hub_source_is_newer() is a model three-valued predicate returning a distinct 2 for every unknown. But health_ok() is two-valued: a curl timeout, a removed curl binary, a hub moved off :8100 and a genuinely dead hub are one value, and cmd_loop restarts on it. Separately, check_hub_stale_source is called only from cmd_once and never from cmd_loop — the C42 bug the bus supervisor already fixed — while the header claims the running supervisor now notices a stale hub. Not edited from here: the hub supervisor is a long-running script and editing a running .sh is its own incident class.

observers.reason: FIXED, not deferred — reviewed 2026-08-23. The fail-OPEN pipeline ('pgrep | xargs … || true' summed to 0GB on every failure mode) was replaced 2026-08-12 (commit 381dddfe6) and completed here: NIGHTSHIFT_GUARD_STATE is three-valued (measured <N>GB / honest 0 / failed); pgrep-missing and pgrep rc>=2 are `failed`; all-VmRSS-reads-failed is `failed`; and the second (MemAvailable) channel being unreadable is now `failed` too — one negative and one blind eye is not a clear, and the polarity rule ('for EXCLUSION, unknown must mean busy', inference_load_check.py) is stated in-file. run_wrapper.sh (row nightshift_run_wrapper) exits 4 unless state=measured. NOT battery-adoptable: it is a sourced measurement library, not a daemon watchdog — its target (RAM-resident inference) publishes no pid/heartbeat, the harness's heartbeat-pid + proc-scan shape cannot be attached honestly, and its corrective action lives entirely in its consumer.

FIXED, not deferred — reviewed 2026-08-23. autopilot_running() was the specimen verbatim ('pgrep -f scripts/autopilot/autopilot.py start' — any flag between the path and 'start' read as 'AutoPilot not running' and lab shadow jobs launched into a live AutoPilot). It is now three-valued (running|stopped|unconfirmed): the authoritative channel is the singleton flock on orchestration/.autopilot.lock (held by construction — orchestrator state_ownership.py — argv-independent), corroborated by adjacency-robust dual pgrep patterns (autopilot.py <flags> start + autopilot_supervisor.py, mirroring inference_load_check.py and start_authority_daemon.py); unconfirmed SUPPRESSES the shadow launch (unknown means busy). The three 'missing cross-repo path -> skip -> return 0' branches now report AUX-DEPENDENCY-MISSING and exit 5 (partial run) instead of a clean 0. NOT battery-adoptable: it is a systemd-timer launcher, not a daemon watchdog — its only observation gates a side feed, its target publishes a flock rather than a pid heartbeat, and the harness's heartbeat-pid shape does not attach. Its guard refusal (exit 4) is regression-tested by scripts/nightshift/tests/test_inference_guard.sh.

FIXED, not deferred — reviewed 2026-08-23. The preflight green-lit a bench against a live AutoPilot: an EMPTY pgrep result read as a positive 'no AutoPilot', and a missing pgrep binary raised FileNotFoundError out of run() before the (0,1)-returncode handling was reached. autopilot_state() is now three-valued (present|absent|unobservable), mirroring inference_load_check.py: FileNotFoundError is caught (missing binary = unobservable); an empty pattern result is NEVER trusted alone — a negative requires the singleton flock (orchestration/.autopilot.lock) to be provably free too; argv drift reads as present (the drifted daemon still holds the lock), closing the reference implementation's named residual; and unobservable FAILS the preflight in both strict and advisory modes ('for EXCLUSION, unknown must mean busy'). NOT battery-adoptable: it is a one-shot Python preflight, not a daemon watchdog — the harness drives `/bin/bash <script> observe` against a heartbeat file this script has no production relationship to.

observers.notes: `pgrep -f "claude"` is a bare substring matching any argv containing 'claude', including its own caller. `pgrep -f "monitor_storage"` makes a renamed/relocated monitor read as permanently absent, so the check permanently recommends starting a second one. Several probes use `|| echo unknown` and then COMPARE 'unknown' against the expected value, reporting FAIL — an unreadable /sys node in a container is scored as a misconfiguration. Report-only, but it gates session start.

observers.reason: FIXED, not deferred — reviewed 2026-08-23. The committed `sudo pkill -f claude` (and its `pgrep -f claude`) is DELETED: on a shared host a 'claude' substring is a wildcard over every session's argv, including the script's own caller, and the PreToolUse pattern-kill hook inspects the typed command, not the script body, so the rule was assumed-enforced. The script now refuses to stop processes by pattern and prints the operator steps for killing only pids they verified themselves (ps -eo pid,etime,cmd | grep -i '[c]laude'; kill <verified-pid>); the unmount step reports a busy mount explicitly instead of aborting under set -e, and the delete prompt warns that a live bind mount makes rm go through to /mnt/raid0/llm/tmp/claude. Exempt as interactive operator tooling: a human-run, one-shot cleanup utility that takes no observation-based decision (it now refuses to guess) — out of the watchdog class the battery guards, and outside the daemon-supervisor lifecycle the contract enforces.

observers.notes: Enrolled BY HAND: neither discovery rule finds it (it identifies no process by argv, so Rule A misses it, and it does not source observer_guard.sh, so Rule B does too). REWRITTEN AT P3-3 (2026-08-16): the pane-text heuristics were DELETED — STUCK-INPUT, IDLE-CANDIDATE, DETECTOR-BLIND, PANE-UNREADABLE/DEAD and FLEET-UNREADABLE are gone, because 2,499 of 2,654 STUCK-INPUT reports (94%) were the agent CLI's own empty-composer placeholder text. It no longer decides anything about a session's liveness; per-recipient liveness belongs to the daemon (P0-2b) and pool-runner liveness to P3-4. What remains is hardware- and bus-grounded: COMPUTE-IDLE (rocm-smi + region claims, escalated only when compute-gated READY rows are waiting) and QUEUE-AGING (READY rows past a threshold with worker capacity free, classified by the gate refusing them — every refusal class has an owner and a routed fix). Its internal discipline is still three-valued: fw_classify_compute returns 'unknown' and never collapses it to idle, an unreadable queue is reported as QUEUE-UNREADABLE rather than as an empty one, and a domain that could not be read is excluded from the alarm clear sweep. Alarms go to alarm_channel.py (emit-once-on-state-change); pane capture survives ONLY as clearly-labelled human evidence attached to an already-decided alarm, OFF by default. What is missing for v1 is the uniform `observe` entrypoint and the behavioural battery. Takes no corrective action of any kind: it detects and logs, never sends keys, never writes the bus, never kills.

observers.reason: REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION, not a gap. _pgrep returns None for 'tool unavailable' and every consumer routes that to unconfirmed/pgrep_missing; mi210_state fails closed to device_state 'unknown'; is_quiet_window names each unconfirmable signal in its reason list. It states the polarity rule this whole contract encodes: 'for EXCLUSION, unknown must mean busy; for ACCUSATION, unknown must mean silence.' Residual (argv drift reads as a positive 'none' rather than unconfirmed) is recorded under OBS-5's neighbourhood, not enforced here.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION. daemon_liveness returns True|False|None, handles PermissionError as alive-under-another-uid, and returns True-with-the-doubt-stated when identity is unverifiable; heartbeat_freshness keeps liveness and freshness on separate axes. This is the standard the rest of the repo is being held to.
